agree.reason: Staff who have worked at their branch for ten years or more and don't want phone work get a clear, respectful notice, but nothing concrete enough to keep them: no exact pay increase, no seniority rule for shifts, no six-month way back to severance, and only placeholder dates.

honest.reason: It leaves out the 'better for everyone' claim and makes up no numbers, though 'puts pressure on everyone who answers those calls' and 'will make a real difference' go slightly past what the facts show.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are repeated as given, with nothing worked out from them: severance is never turned into a real amount (for example, 20 weeks of pay for ten years), and 'same pay or higher' stays vague when the actual raise is $1.50 an hour.

right_comparison.reason: It uses the 44% drop in visits and the 60% rise in phone and chat contacts to explain why the branches are closing, and it states the leaving option accurately, but it doesn't make that choice concrete with real amounts or with what working in the center would involve compared with that option.

qualification.reason: The key commitments, including the decision deadline, the shift rules and the meeting dates, appear as bracketed [DATE] placeholders, even though February 14 and March 1 were available, so the reader has nothing to check.

objections.reason: It admits the change in hours, but it never mentions the two weeks of rumours, says nothing to people who don't want phone work, and leaves out answers that were available: senior staff choose shifts first, and anyone who leaves within six months can still take severance.

fit.reason: It is roughly the requested length and reads as an email from the COO, but its many bracketed placeholders, including a missing name, mean it isn't ready to send.
